sections.html:
Linn County occupies the middle of the Willamette Valley, and Albany is both the seat and the largest city. The 2020 census counted 128,610 residents, a 10.2% gain over 2010, across 2,309 square miles. The county was created on December 28, 1847. Housing units numbered 51,921 in 2020, and 66.1% were owner-occupied.

Towns include Albany, Lebanon, Sweet Home, Brownsville, Harrisburg, Halsey, Scio, Tangent, Millersburg, Lyons and Sodaville, plus parts of Gates, Idanha and Mill City. About 34.2% of residents live in rural areas, so plenty of sellers own acreage, a shop or a farm house.

Schools take the largest share. For the 2024 assessment year, the county's notice split the tax this way:

  • Schools: 41.7%
  • County: 23.5%
  • Cities: 23%
  • Rural fire districts: 7%
  • Urban renewal: 3.2%
  • Miscellaneous: 1.6%

Voters also approved changes in several districts. Jefferson Rural Fire District added a local option levy of $0.81 per $1,000 of assessed value, and Sweet Home Fire and Ambulance District set a new bond rate of $0.46 per $1,000. A Sweet Home law enforcement levy of $7.85 per $1,000 followed two years of under-levying. A house in Sweet Home and one in Albany can therefore carry quite different rates.

Bills go out by October 25. Pay in full by November 15 and you get a 3% discount. Pay two-thirds by then for 2% off, with the last third due May 15. The one-third plan carries no discount, with payments on November 15, in February and in May. The Tax Collector sends no reminders for the February or May payments, and any statement under $40 must be paid in full.

  • Mail a check or money order to Linn County Tax Collector, PO Box 100, Albany, OR 97321. Never mail cash.
  • Pay in person at Room 214, Linn County Courthouse, 300 4th Avenue SW, Albany.
  • Use the drop box at the courthouse's west (Ferry Street) entrance, on the left side of the doors.
  • Pay online by card or e-check.

A postmark counts toward the discount, but a returned check can forfeit it. Payments go to the earliest year still owed.

Delinquency notices go out between May 16 and May 25. A property that has been delinquent for three years lands on the foreclosure list around July 16. The list is usually published around August 16, and final judgment follows around September 16. The oldest delinquent year has to be paid to pull a property off the list.

Two years of redemption follow judgment. An owner who redeems pays the taxes, a 5% penalty, interest and a fee, and any surplus above the debt belongs to the owner after the county takes the property.

For a payoff figure, call 541-967-3808 during business hours. A title company will ask for it before closing on a Linn County sale.

sections.h2: Recording rules at the Clerk's office
sections.html:
The Clerk records deeds from 8:30 AM to 4:00 PM at 300 4th Ave. SW in Albany. Anything received between 4:00 and 5:00 PM is recorded the next business day.

  • The first page needs a blank 3 inch by 2 inch space for the recording tag, and text of at least 10 point.
  • It must show the return name and address, every party's name, the consideration, and a "Send Tax Statements To" name and address.
  • Deeds cost $105.00 for the first page, plus $5.00 for each added page.
  • A document that fails the first-page rules and is fixed from elsewhere in the paper costs a $20.00 non-compliance fee.

Call the Clerk at 541-967-3829 with questions before you sign.

If you think the market value on your statement is too high, call the Assessor at 541-967-3808 first. Many questions get answered with one conversation, and the staff can explain how the figure was reached. If you still disagree, the Property Value Appeal Board is the place to file, and the deadline is December 31. Do not wait for the last week, because you will want time to gather sales of similar houses and photos of any defects.

Farm use is taxed under a special assessment that values land by income instead of market value. Disqualified land can owe extra tax for up to 10 years, or five inside an urban growth boundary. Ending farm use, leaving an exclusive farm use zone, or approval of a nonfarm dwelling can trigger it.

Ask the Linn County Assessor for the special assessment status before you list rural land. Senior and disabled owners can also ask about the state's deferral program, which leaves a lien that is repaid at sale. The county keeps a page on the Senior or Disabled Citizen Deferral program.

sections.h2: Wildfire and wet-season wear on homes
sections.html:
Albany gets about 39.89 inches of precipitation a year, with December the wettest month. Sweet Home, nearer the Cascades, gets about 54.45 inches, mostly from October through March, so moss, drainage and crawlspace moisture are the usual inspection items there.

Wildfire touched the eastern edge of the county in 2020. The Santiam Fire burned 402,274 acres across Marion, Linn, Jefferson and Clackamas counties. Detroit and Gates were nearly destroyed, Idanha and Mill City were damaged, and more than 1,500 structures were lost.

sections.h2: Selling a Linn County house with a tax balance
sections.html:
A balance does not stop a sale. Here is the usual path:

  • Call the Assessor at 541-967-3808 for a payoff figure.
  • Give the figure to the title company.
  • Escrow pays the oldest year first, because payments are credited that way, and settles the rest from your proceeds.

A cash buyer skips lender appraisals and repair conditions, which helps when a farm house or a shop has deferred work. Bring your deed, the latest statement and, for acreage, the special assessment status to your first meeting. Plan the calendar around the payment dates. A closing in late October or early November means the November 15 installment is about to come due, so settle in the contract who pays it. A closing in spring puts the May 15 installment in play, and the Tax Collector sends no reminder for it.

faqs.q: What is the county seat of Linn County, Oregon?
faqs.a: Albany, which is also the largest city. An 1851 territorial act moved the seat there, and a special election in 1856 confirmed it.

faqs.q: When are Linn County property taxes due?
faqs.a: November 15 for a full payment or the first installment. The remaining installments are due February 15 and May 15, and statements are mailed by October 25.

faqs.q: How do I pay Linn County property tax in person?
faqs.a: Go to Room 214 of the Linn County Courthouse, 300 4th Avenue SW in Albany, or use the drop box at the west (Ferry Street) entrance. Checks go to Linn County Tax Collector.

faqs.q: When is the Linn County property tax appeal deadline?
faqs.a: December 31. File with the Property Value Appeal Board, and call the Assessor at 541-967-3808 with questions first.

faqs.q: How long can Linn County taxes go unpaid before foreclosure?
faqs.a: Three years. Property delinquent that long goes on a list around July 16, and judgment follows about two months later. After that the owner has a two-year redemption period.
